title: Metal data table and design brief
subject: Science
unit: Summer 1: Metals and their uses (8G); energy transfers (8K)
source: Seeded from science/y8 lesson 50 (Metal data table and design brief (portal worksheet))
intro: Lesson 50: Choosing the right metal: a design brief. To understand how to use data on properties, reactivity and cost to choose a metal for a job

questions.q: Choose a material for a ship's propeller in seawater. Justify with data.
questions.a: e.g. stainless steel or a bronze alloy: strong with very good corrosion resistance
questions.model: List the needs: strong, constant seawater, so corrosion resistance matters most. Stainless steel: high strength, very good resistance.

questions.q: Why is titanium not used for everything?

questions.a: Balancing needs when no material is perfect

questions.q: Design brief: choose materials for the sea footbridge, its handrails and its electrical lighting cables. Justify each in the portal response box with data. Starter: 'For the ... I chose ... because ...'
questions.a: Justified choices, e.g. bridge: stainless or galvanised painted steel; cables: copper; rails: stainless steel
questions.model: Teacher models the lighting cables: 'copper, because it is the best conductor here and its low strength does not matter inside a cable'.

questions.q: Give one drawback of each choice and how you would manage it.
questions.a: e.g. steel rusts: galvanise and paint

questions.q: Why might recycled aluminium be a good choice for the environment?
questions.a: Recycling uses much less energy than extracting new metal

questions.q: Big question: what worries you most about a sea footbridge metal?
questions.a: Corrosion from salt water, plus strength and cost.
